name: Devil's Dyke hillfort, Poynings
source: Atlas of Hillforts, record 3741; English Wikipedia: Devil's Dyke, Sussex
note: Used as a defensive site before and after the Iron Age (Atlas of Hillforts: Devil's Dyke, Poynings). Legend: the Devil dug a trench through the Downs so that the sea would drown the Christians of the Weald; St Cuthman of Steyning fooled him with a candle and a crowing cock, and he fled, leaving the dyke unfinished.

label: Devil's Dyke
name: Devil's Dyke, Cambridgeshire
note: In medieval times it was simply called the dic (the ditch), le Micheldyche or magnum fossatum (great ditch). Thought most likely Anglo-Saxon, by analogy with Fleam Dyke (AD 330 to 510).
